## How to evaluate Swarmia against Waydev


Swarmia is a developer productivity and team improvement platform. Product scope, enterprise controls, AI metrics, and supported integrations change over time; claims that a capability is absent require current documentation or a direct vendor confirmation.


**Best-fit decision:** Evaluate Swarmia for team-level delivery visibility and continuous improvement practices. Evaluate Waydev for engineering intelligence across delivery, AI adoption, AI cost and resource allocation. Require each vendor to demonstrate the same workflow with your own data.


**Source:**[Swarmia product information / related primary reference](https://swarmia.com/) .[Waydev research methodology](https://waydev.co/engineering-ai-index-2027/) ·[Waydev Brain](https://waydev.co/waydev-brain/) .


Feature availability, pricing, contractual terms and deployment options should be verified directly. This is a Waydev-authored comparison, not an independent certification.


## Swarmia alternatives, competitors and replacement checklist


**Comparing a Swarmia replacement?** Start with what your teams actually use: DORA and PR flow, developer surveys, AI coding adoption/cost, investment reporting and team reporting.[Swarmia currently offers AI adoption and spend insights, DevEx surveys and software capitalization](https://www.swarmia.com/product/) ; these are not exclusive Waydev differentiators.


- **Stay with / evaluate Swarmia** when its workflow insights, research-backed surveys and self-service reporting match your needs.
- **Evaluate Waydev** when you need an enterprise engineering intelligence layer bringing DORA, SPACE and DX together with Signals, Goals, Prompt Dashboards and[private air-gapped Waydev Brain](https://waydev.co/waydev-brain/) .
- **Compare pricing fairly:** Request current vendor quotes and account for onboarding, hosting, support, AI-tool coverage, historical data migration and minimum seats. Waydev enterprise pricing is private.


**Migration proof:** Export a representative team’s PR, sprint, incident, AI usage and developer-feedback data; reconcile metric definitions and check the new baseline. See the[Swarmia migration guide](https://waydev.co/outgrowing-swarmia-a-migration-guide-for-engineering-orgs-that-scaled/) , or[ask for a Waydev POC](https://waydev.co/demo/) .

## Waydev is built for the org Swarmia was not designed to reach


Both platforms read your engineering stack and both do DORA well. The gap opens at enterprise scale: deployment inside your own perimeter, source control beyond the big three, metrics you define yourself, and contributor-level visibility that Swarmia declines to provide by design.


If your engineering organization is large, regulated, or running a mixed toolchain, that gap is the entire decision.[Request an enterprise demo](https://waydev.co/demo/) and see it on your own repositories.


**20,000** *contributors in a single tenant, per Waydev’s enterprise specification*


**40+** *documented integrations across Git, planning, CI and AI tooling*


**On-prem** *self-hosted or cloud, your choice*


## Where the two platforms actually differ


A fair starting point. Most of the core is shared, so the decision lives in the two outer bands.


## Six reasons enterprise teams pick Waydev


Deployment


### Your commit data never has to leave your perimeter


Waydev runs cloud or on-premise, with self-hosted Git and ticketing integrations on the Enterprise plan. Swarmia operates as a cloud service. For banks, healthcare, defence suppliers and anyone with a data residency clause, this ends the evaluation before feature lists open.


Coverage


### The whole toolchain, not the popular part of it


Azure DevOps, GitLab Enterprise, AWS CodeCommit and Gerrit alongside GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket, plus Jira, Azure Boards and ClickUp. Swarmia’s published integrations centre on GitHub, GitLab, Jira and Linear. Large organizations rarely have one clean stack, and the repositories a platform cannot read are exactly the ones hiding your bottleneck.


Customization


### Metrics you define, not metrics you select


Write your own formulas, build dashboards from the widget set, and produce reports across large datasets. Selecting from a fixed library works until leadership asks the question the library does not answer.


Visibility


### Contributor-level insight when you need it


Swarmia takes a deliberate position against measuring individuals and builds accordingly. Waydev gives you[work log](https://waydev.co/features/work-log/) and contributor insights for understanding load distribution, onboarding progress and where knowledge is concentrated, with role-based access controlling who can see what. It is a real philosophical difference, and it matters most when a leader has to answer a specific question about a specific team.


Scale


### Built for ten thousand contributors, not ten teams


Role and stats management, team-level permissions, SSO and SAML, and an open API that both pulls and pushes so engineering data feeds the warehouse and the board deck you already maintain.


AI


### AI impact measured, not just AI seats counted


[Waydev Brain](https://waydev.co/waydev-brain/) and[Signals](https://waydev.co/features/signals/) surface where AI tooling is moving throughput, review load and quality, and generate targets and notifications from it. Adoption percentages are easy. Attribution is the hard part, and it is the part a CFO asks about.


Both tools will tell you your cycle time. Only one will do it inside your own infrastructure, across your whole estate, on metrics you wrote yourself.

### Where Swarmia is the better call


Worth saying plainly, because a comparison nobody believes converts nobody.


- You have fewer than ten developers. Swarmia’s free plan covers most of its standard features at that size, and no paid platform beats free.
- You want a strictly team-level culture with no individual data in the system at all, and you want the tool to enforce that rather than trust configuration.
- Your stack is GitHub plus Jira or Linear, you are cloud-first, and Slack-native nudges and working agreements are the workflow you want.

**Automation** Targets, notifications and burnout alerts to Slack, Google Chat or Microsoft Teams, plus the[activity heatmap](https://waydev.co/features/activity-heatmap/) for working rhythms and anomalies.

## Switching from Swarmia


**1. Prove it on your own repositories** The proof of concept runs against your real history, so the comparison uses your numbers rather than a demo tenant.


**2. Keep the history you already have** Waydev backfills existing version control and issue tracking data, up to 6 months on Pro and 36 months on Premium, so trend lines start immediately.


**3. Check the repositories Swarmia could not read** If part of your estate sits on Azure DevOps, Gerrit or AWS CodeCommit, connect those first. That is usually where the missing picture was.


**4. Plan the rollout with a person** A dedicated customer success and adoption team handles onboarding and ongoing use rather than leaving it to a help centre article.

## Common questions


### Does Swarmia offer on-premise deployment?


No. Swarmia operates as a cloud service. Waydev offers self-hosted and on-premise integrations on the Enterprise plan, which is the single most common reason enterprises move.


### Is Swarmia’s data delayed?


No, and we have removed an earlier version of this page that implied otherwise. Swarmia states that its data updates in real time.1 Refresh speed is not a differentiator between these two platforms.


### Is SOC 3 a higher certification than SOC 2?


No. A SOC 3 report can only be issued after a clean SOC 2 Type II audit and is a public summary of that same examination.4 Waydev holds SOC 2 Type II and publishes a SOC 3, so our attestation can be shared without an NDA. Swarmia is also SOC 2 Type 2.3 Both are secure platforms and the difference is in how the report is shared.


### Why does Waydev show contributor-level data when Swarmia does not?


Because some questions are about a person and cannot be answered at team level, including onboarding progress, review load concentration and knowledge risk. Waydev gates that behind role-based access so it supports managers rather than exposing rankings. Swarmia’s position is that individual data should not exist in the system. Both views are defensible. Yours should decide the tool.


### Can we migrate historical data?


Yes. Waydev backfills up to 6 months of history on Pro and 36 months on Premium.

## Why choose Waydev over Swarmia in 2027?


**Where Waydev stands out:** Evaluate proactive Signals, measurable Goals and a private AI intelligence layer alongside Swarmia’s existing AI ROI and DevEx capabilities. Compare capabilities through a pilot; no single vendor is universally best.


### 1. Waydev Brain: your own private AI intelligence layer


**Waydev 15B** is Waydev’s proprietary 15-billion-parameter model for the software development lifecycle.[Waydev Brain](https://waydev.co/the-ai-labs-have-a-unit-metric-most-engineering-orgs-still-dont/) supports private, fully **air-gapped enterprise deployment** , with its model, agents and engineering intelligence running inside the customer’s environment. Confirm deployment scope and requirements during a security evaluation.


### 2. Waydev Agent: ask questions against engineering data


[Waydev Agent](https://waydev.co/features/waydev-agent/) answers natural-language questions about delivery, AI cost, PR activity and trends, with inspectable supporting queries for analysis. Specialized skills and[Agent Registry](https://waydev.co/features/agent-registry/) help organizations understand AI agents and their owners.


### 3. Signals and AI Goals: turn measurement into action


[Signals](https://waydev.co/features/signals/) proactively check engineering data for issues that warrant attention;[Goals](https://waydev.co/features/goals/) set measurable targets and track progress by team or organization. Examples include review bottlenecks, code-quality risk and changes in AI-related spend.


### 4. Prompt Dashboards: create editable reports by asking


Describe a question such as “Show AI spend, cycle time and rework by team.”[Prompt Dashboards](https://waydev.co/features/prompt-dashboards/) can assemble Waydev metrics into editable, shareable dashboards using common definitions.


### 5. AI Adoption, Impact, ROI and governance


Evaluate AI-assisted work by tool, team and initiative, combining usage and costs with delivery and quality signals.[AI Governance and Limits](https://waydev.co/features/ai-governance-and-limits/) adds spend alerts, policy controls and an audit trail. AI usage is not, by itself, proof of ROI.

## How to choose a Swarmia alternative in 2027


**Updated buyer’s verdict (October 2026):** Choose Swarmia for a closer look if its AI spend and team-throughput model matches your management workflow. Evaluate Waydev alongside it if you need an alternative engineering intelligence view that joins AI adoption, DORA, developer experience and executive reporting.


**What Swarmia already does:** Swarmia added an AI Impact ROI view in August 2026, including AI cost, developer cost, throughput per FTE and cost per work unit. It also offers team-level breakdowns. It would be inaccurate to say Swarmia cannot measure AI ROI.[Check the competitor’s own documentation](https://www.swarmia.com/changelog/2026-08-07-ai-roi/) .


**What to test in a proof of value:** Compare the same teams and calendar period; ask both vendors to reconcile token pricing, FTE cost assumptions and production outcomes. A lower cost per PR is not automatically a lower cost per delivered customer value.


### Does Swarmia calculate AI ROI?


Yes. Its August 2026 ROI tab reports AI and developer costs alongside delivered work. Ask how each calculation relates to your financial definition of ROI.


**Evidence standard:** These are editorial assessments, not a validated hands-on benchmark. Feature availability, pricing and implementation requirements may differ by plan or configuration. Request the same live demonstration and measure with identical definitions before selecting either vendor.


**Decision in brief:** Prioritize a platform that can demonstrate impact using your organization’s real engineering data. During the trial, evaluate team-level AI adoption, cost, delivery impact, survey feedback and governance. Avoid comparing platforms on a single dashboard screenshot or vendor marketing claims.


### What Swarmia offers today


Swarmia publicly describes AI adoption and cost analysis, delivery impact, developer-experience surveys, and software capitalization. It should not be described as a tool that only counts pull requests.[Vendor source and product details](https://www.swarmia.com/software-engineering-intelligence-platform/) .

### Five criteria for a fair enterprise comparison


1. **Delivery evidence:** Require consistent definitions for cycle time, deployment frequency, change failures and rework.
2. **AI impact and ROI:** Separate licensed seats and AI usage from verified production outcomes and fully loaded costs.
3. **Developer experience:** Assess friction, review queues, qualitative feedback and whether metrics discourage gaming.
4. **Enterprise fit:** Validate integrations, role-based access, data retention, security reviews and deployment constraints.
5. **Proof of value:** Agree on a baseline, real teams and success criteria before starting a pilot.


### Questions to ask in a Swarmia vs Waydev demo


- Can we compare AI tool spend with delivery impact across teams and repositories?
- Which delivery and quality measures can the evaluation connect to AI adoption?
- How are surveys, organizational changes and historical data handled?


### When is Waydev worth evaluating?


Consider Waydev when you need to investigate DORA and developer-experience trends alongside AI adoption, delivery outcomes and business impact. The right choice depends on your workflow, integrations, governance and which outcomes you need to prove; request a side-by-side pilot using your own data rather than relying on blanket feature claims.
